tools.name: search_essays
tools.description: Search the essays of Niels Langereis on AI adoption, organisational change, the politics of AI, junior formation and judgement, brand and AI agents, boards and governance. Returns titles, dates, summaries, a matching snippet and links. For a plain list of every essay use list_essays. Follow up with get_essay for the full text before quoting him.

query.description: Topic or question, e.g. 'who owns AI decisions', 'brand lock-in by AI agents'. Empty lists everything.

tools.name: get_essay
tools.description: Get the full text of one essay by Niels Langereis, as Markdown, with its date, site link and the original LinkedIn link. Use the id from search_essays or list_essays, or a title.

id.description: Essay id (from search_essays) or its title

tools.name: get_enterprise_ai_map
tools.description: Niels Langereis's enterprise AI map: 24 illustrative AI agents across ten business functions (strategy, product, design, marketing, sales, customer success, operations, people, finance, data and IT), each with its rollout phase, what it optimises for and the trade-off it creates for other functions; plus the coordination layer, the bench and the external renderers that decide whether faster work becomes a better organisation. Use it to reason about someone's own AI rollout. detail='summary' returns only the skeleton (functions, agents, phases and trade-offs, plus one line per remaining part), which is enough for most reasoning; detail='full' (default) adds the complete prose on coordination, the bench and the renderers. Optionally filter by function or phase. Shows an interactive map where the client supports it.

function.description: Optional: focus on one function, e.g. 'Marketing and growth', 'Finance'.

phase.description: Optional: p1 co-pilots, p2 brains, p3 autonomous agents.

detail.description: summary: functions, agents and trade-offs only. full (default): also the prose on coordination, the bench and the renderers.

tools.name: get_skill_matrix_method
tools.description: Explains Niels Langereis's skill-matrix gap analysis: a competency matrix run for formation rather than efficiency, to find where AI has removed the work that used to turn juniors into seniors. Includes the status rule, how to read it, a worked example and credits. Use before run_skill_matrix if the user wants to understand the method first.

tools.name: run_skill_matrix
tools.description: Runs Niels Langereis's skill-matrix gap analysis for one role and shows it as an interactive matrix the user can edit (who does the work now, bench depth, formation actions). Draft 6 to 10 competencies for the user's role yourself from what you know about it, spanning routine work AI can now do with senior oversight, work AI already runs autonomously, and judgement work that needs a human. Set bench (how many people can do it at the strategic level) from what the user told you; if unknown, use 1 and say it is an estimate they should correct. Omit competencies to show the generic analyst example. The result flags 'At risk' (human work, one person deep), 'Thin' (two deep) and 'Reps gone' (AI runs it autonomously, so the formation that used to happen in reviewing it has gone too: ask where juniors get those reps now). After the user edits, their current matrix arrives in your context.

role.description: The role being analysed, e.g. 'Marketing manager at a 200-person B2B firm'.

execution.description: What it looks like at execution level.

who.description: Who does it now. AI + oversight: AI does it, a person reviews. AI autonomous: AI runs it end to end, nobody reviews (phase 3 on the enterprise AI map). Human: needs a human touch.

formation_action.description: How juniors still get formed here: the second loop.

bench.description: People who can do it at strategic level. Only for Human work.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Who Niels Langereis is and how to work with him: what he does and for whom, how he works, his background, his talks and speaking, and how to get in touch. Use when someone asks whether he could help them, wants to hire or book him, or wants his background. Contact is by email or the site's contact form; this server does not send messages.

tools.name: list_essays
tools.description: List every published essay by Niels Langereis, newest first, with id, date, one-line summary and links. Use to see what he has written before choosing one, or when the user asks for his essays, his latest piece or everything on a theme. Follow up with get_essay for the full text.

limit.description: Maximum number of essays to return. Default: all.

tools.name: list_talks
tools.description: List the talks and keynotes Niels Langereis offers, with languages, practical details and how to book him. Use when an organiser, event planner or company is looking for a speaker on AI adoption, the politics of AI, junior formation and judgement, brands chosen by AI assistants, or intellectual property in generative AI.

tools.name: list_appearances
tools.description: List recent public appearances by Niels Langereis (podcasts, video panels, talks) with outlet, date, language, host, co-guests, a link to the platform's own page, and a short summary of the positions Niels himself took. The summaries cover only his views, not the other speakers', and are not transcripts. Use when someone asks what he said somewhere, where he has appeared, or wants to hear or watch him before booking.

id.description: Optional appearance id from a previous list to return just that one.
